dims: anyone (“When anyone of you offers an offering”)
from the herd: a male without defect, at the door of the Tent of Meeting; he lays his hand on its head
from the flock: a male without defect, of the sheep or of the goats
of birds: turtledoves or young pigeons
from the herd or the flock: all of it: the pieces, the head and the fat, and the innards and legs washed with water
of birds: the whole bird, torn by its wings but not divided; its crop with its filth is cast beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes
the fire: kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out
from the herd or the flock: sprinkled around on the altar by Aaron's sons, the priests
of birds: drained out on the side of the altar
no one: none of it: the priest burns all of it
the skin: the priest who offers it has the skin for himself
the ashes: the priest, in his linen garment and his linen breeches, puts them beside the altar; then he puts on other garments and carries them outside the camp to a clean place

freewill or required: Leviticus 1 names no occasion (“When anyone of you offers an offering”); the text requires it in the continual burnt offering, morning and evening (Exod 29:38-42), as the second bird of the sin offering (Lev 5:10), and on the Day of Atonement (16:3)
items.note: An offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahweh (1:9). Two lambs were to be offered as a continual burnt offering, one in the morning and one at evening (Exod 29:38-42). The fire on the altar is never to go out (6:12-13).

dims: anyone (“When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering”)
of fine flour: fine flour, with oil poured on it and frankincense put on it
baked in the oven: unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil
on a griddle: unleavened fine flour mixed with oil, cut in pieces, with oil poured on it
of the pan: fine flour with oil
of first fruits: grain in the ear parched with fire, bruised grain of the fresh ear, with oil and frankincense
every one: seasoned with salt; no meal offering is made with yeast, and no yeast or honey is burned as an offering made by fire
the priests' own: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, half in the morning and half in the evening, made with oil in a griddle, in the day when he is anointed
of fine flour: a handful of its fine flour and its oil, with all its frankincense, as its memorial
of the oven, griddle or pan: its memorial
of first fruits: part of its bruised grain and part of its oil, with all its frankincense, as its memorial
the priests' own: all of it
Aaron and his sons: what is left, without yeast, in a holy place, the court of the Tent of Meeting; every male among them
the priest who offers it: one baked in the oven, or dressed in the pan or on the griddle
all the sons of Aaron: one mixed with oil, or dry
a priest's own: every meal offering of a priest is wholly burned; it shall not be eaten

freewill or required: Leviticus 2 names no occasion (“When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering”); the text requires one with each lamb of the continual burnt offering (Exod 29:40-41), and the priests' own, perpetually (Lev 6:20)
items.note: It has no blood. What is left of it is most holy (2:3; 6:17). Yeast and honey may be offered as first fruits, but they shall not rise up for a pleasant aroma on the altar (2:11-12).

dims: from the herd: male or female, without defect
from the flock, a lamb: male or female, without defect
from the flock, a goat: a goat
for a thanksgiving: with it, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, cakes mixed with oil, and cakes of leavened bread
the one who offers it: brings the fat with the breast with his own hands
from the herd, or a goat: the fat that covers the innards and all the fat on them, the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver
a lamb: the same, and the entire tail fat, taken away close to the backbone
every one: sprinkled around on the altar by Aaron's sons
Aaron and his sons: the breast, waved for a wave offering
the priest who sprinkles the blood: the right thigh, a heave offering, and one of each kind of the thanksgiving cakes
everyone who is clean: the meat: a thanksgiving's on its day, a vow's or a freewill offering's by the next day
all the fat, and the blood: Yahweh's: Israel eats no fat of bull, sheep or goat, and no blood of bird or animal
on the third day: what remains of the meat is burned with fire
unclean: meat that touches any unclean thing is burned with fire
for a thanksgiving, or a vow, or a freewill offering
items.note: All the fat is Yahweh's; Israel eats neither fat nor blood (3:16-17; 7:22-27). That the one who offers it eats the meat is the text's “everyone who is clean may eat it” (7:19). The waved breast and the heaved thigh are the anointing portion of Aaron and his sons, their portion forever (7:34-36).

dims: the anointed priest: a young bull without defect
the whole congregation: a young bull; the elders lay their hands on its head
a ruler: a goat, a male without defect
one of the common people: a goat, a female without defect, or a lamb, a female without defect
one guilty of 5:1–4: a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, after he confesses
can't afford a lamb: two turtledoves, or two young pigeons: one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering
can't afford two turtledoves: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, with no oil and no frankincense

a bull: all its fat: the fat that covers the innards and all the fat on them, the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, as it is taken from the peace offerings; on the altar of burnt offering
a goat or a lamb: all its fat, as it is taken from the peace offerings
two birds: the second is offered for a burnt offering
fine flour: a handful as the memorial portion

the anointed priest's and the congregation's bull: brought into the Tent of Meeting and sprinkled seven times before the veil, put on the horns of the altar of sweet incense; the rest poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offering

the congregation's bull: put on the horns of the altar which is before Yahweh, that is in the Tent of Meeting (the altar of sweet incense, 4:7); the rest poured out at the base of the altar of burnt offering
a ruler's or one of the people's: put on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; the rest poured out at its base
a bird: sprinkled on the side of the altar; the rest drained out at its base
the priest who offers it: in a holy place, the court of the Tent of Meeting; every male among the priests
the priest: the rest of the fine flour, as the meal offering
a young bull: the anointed priest's and the congregation's bull: its skin, meat, head, legs, innards and dung, carried outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burned
blood brought in: no sin offering whose blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement is eaten: it is burned with fire
required: when anyone sins unintentionally (4:2) and it is made known to him (4:23, 28), or is known (4:14), or when he is guilty of one of these (5:1-5)
items.note: Most holy (6:25, 29). The WEB's 5:6-7 calls what is brought there “his trespass offering”, “for a sin offering”; it is the sin offering's law, and 5:9, 11-12 call it a sin offering, so it is tabled here. Of the two birds, the second is a burnt offering (5:10).

dims: anyone (“If anyone commits a trespass”, “If anyone sins”)

a trespass in the holy things: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation in silver by shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; he makes restitution and adds a fifth part, given to the priest
the silver: the ram's estimation, not a second thing brought
a sin he didn't know: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation
a wrong against his neighbor: he restores it in full and adds a fifth part more, to its owner; then a ram without defect from the flock
the ram: all its fat: the fat tail, the fat that covers the innards, the two kidneys and the fat on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver
the ram: sprinkled around on the altar
every male among the priests: in a holy place; the priest who makes atonement with it has it
required: for a trespass in the holy things, a sin he didn't know, or a wrong against his neighbor; with restitution and a fifth part more where something was taken (5:16; 6:5)
items.note: Most holy (7:1, 6). “As is the sin offering, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them” (7:7). It is killed where the burnt offering is killed (7:2).
